checks: Read work_summary, report.json (246 results, now schema-valid: assumptions are lists) and out/q60/summary.csv. Re-tabulated summary.csv: all-baseline, +-350 km/s, 2 components: contrast Xb47 1.63, 00493+00223 1.36; HCN N/S 2.12 vs 1.96. Agrees with the worker's table.

The result depends on the model: with 3 components (extended added) the contrast is 1.93 (Xb47) and 1.62 (00493+00223), and HCN N/S is 2.8/2.6, against 2.1/2.0 for 2 components. That is +-0.3 in contrast and +-0.7 in N/S from model choice alone, larger than the claimed +-0.3 total. The adopted 1.5+-0.3 therefore understates the systematic error.

The uv subsets are not stable. Set C (the 15-25 kl subset in the summary) gives HCN N/S 3.3-4.0 for both projects, and set D is unconstrained (sd 16 in N/S). Those subsets have poor S/N. Quoting 'contrast rises to 2.0+-0.5 at 25-50 kl' rests on them. It cannot be told apart from noise, and the sign of the trend is not established.

The strongest argument, that N/S HCN in 00493 (2.0) matches Xb47 (2.1), is sound as far as it goes. But the work itself shows both nuclei and both lines in 00493/00223 are ~1.5x brighter than Xb47. A common 50% flux offset between projects is far outside the 10-15% ALMA scale error. Calling it 'common, cancels in ratios' is not an explanation. It could be a PB correction, a Gaussian-PB assumption that is wrong, a mosaic-field weighting error, or a real calibration problem. It is also a hint that the fixed-position model is not measuring the same quantity in the two data sets.

The task asked for a per-MS comparison in uv-matched, tapered images using identical settings. That was not done. The uv model with fixed positions is not equivalent to the image apertures that gave 3.7, and the report does not reproduce the 3.7 by any method of its own. Without that, 'the 3.7 is wrong' is only partly demonstrated: the image-plane integrals at 4.5/5.5/7" gave 2.6, which is itself above 1.5.

Excluding Xb47 EB X8300 (HCN N/S 0.5) as failed is justified only weakly. Its N flux is 2-5x low while HCO+ is normal. This needs a spw/phase-centre/field-ID check, not just exclusion, and the contrast should be quoted with and without it.

The Q55 propagation is reasonable and is stated cautiously (undecided, |dlnBF|<3). It is consistent with team-b p0059/p0060 (R32/10 does not exclude excitation-only; column vs excitation undecided). I agree with that conclusion, and it does not depend on whether the contrast is 1.5 or 1.9.

fixes.what: Do the tclean comparison the task asked for. For every 4-3 MS (each EB separately and per OUS), image HCN and HCO+ with identical settings: common uv range (>=8 kl, trimmed to the common coverage), uvtaper to a common beam of about 1.0" and 1.5", the same weighting, the same mask and a common velocity window. Measure N and S with matched circular apertures and a beam-spectrum at the peak, on both PB-corrected and uncorrected maps.
fixes.why: This is what the question asked, and it is the only way to reproduce or refute 3.7 in the same units as the pipeline images. At present the 3.7 is not reproduced by any method, so the explanation (resolved-out S in the ACA mosaic) is a guess.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Matched uvrange and taper, same cell and imsize, restoringbeam='common' or imsmooth to one beam, same-region aperture sums, error from line-free channels in the same aperture. Report per-EB values and sd.

fixes.what: Explain the 1.5x absolute flux offset between 00493/00223 and Xb47. Compare the same-uv-annulus visibility amplitudes of the two data sets, separately for N and S. Check the PB model by fitting without PB and with the 12m 01246 EB, which has a well-defined PB, as anchor. Check the continuum N/S per EB, from line-free channels, which needs no calibrator tables.
fixes.why: A 50% offset beyond the ALMA scale error cannot be left unexplained. If the offset is not purely multiplicative (e.g. N/S-dependent via PB) it changes the contrast. Line-free continuum N/S is a direct per-EB check on flux scale and decorrelation.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Plot amplitude vs uv distance for each EB over a common annulus; compare to the 12m EB. Check the MS header or flux log for the calibrator flux used, if it can be recovered from the ASDM or calibration tables. If not, state it as not recoverable. Continuum should be consistent at the percent level between EBs.

fixes.what: Restate the uncertainty. Quote the contrast with the model systematics included (2 vs 3 components, window width, and with/without the X8300 EB). Drop the claim of a trend with uv radius unless the 25-50 kl errors come from a proper error budget, and say so in the report. State the range, 1.4-1.9, as the result, not 1.5+-0.3.
fixes.why: The model dependence alone (1.63 vs 1.93) is as large as the quoted error. The C/D uv sets have errors of 1-16 in N/S, so the trend is not significant.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Use a model-averaged value with the spread of the models as the systematic term added in quadrature to the inter-EB sd. Test the trend against a null (shuffle EBs or use noise-only line-free channels) before calling it.

fixes.what: Investigate X8300 (inverted HCN N/S) as a diagnostic: check which field, spw, and phase-centre it uses, and whether the N flux loss is a decorrelation or a wrong-position issue. Report the 8 and 7 EB statistics.
fixes.why: If the failure is a position/field problem it can affect other EBs at a lower level. If it is decorrelation, then it affects the flux-scale argument.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Inspect the phase-vs-time on the target, fit the position of the N peak per EB, and compare to the others.

notes_for_questioner: The HCN/HCO+ 4-3 contrast is probably 1.4-1.9 on 1" scales, with the uncertainty dominated by the model. Does the contrast agree with the 3-2 and 1-0 value (1.45+-0.22 at 1", team-b p0059/p0060)? If so, 4-3 adds no new information beyond the 3-2 and 1-0 results. The large offset in absolute flux (1.5x) between OUS needs its own item. The decisive discriminator remains H13CN/HCN at about 2".
